title: Bridge Comparison Schema
purpose: Compare QM-like and GR-like projection domains through source-relation traceability, retained-feature overlap, conflict tracking, and projection-loss accounting without permitting unification or physical derivation claims.
no_unification_guardrail: no QM/GR unification, derivation, replacement, or physics claim; only analog projection behavior

core_definition.canonical_statement: Bridge comparison evaluates projection-domain relationships through shared source traceability, retained-feature overlap, projection-loss differentials, and coherence constraints.
core_definition.non_unification_rule: Comparison coherence does not imply physical equivalence, source identity, or unification.

comparison_dimensions.name: source_relation_traceability
comparison_dimensions.definition: Measures whether compared projection domains declare compatible ⇔R source relations.

comparison_dimensions.name: retained_feature_overlap
comparison_dimensions.definition: Measures overlap between projection-retained feature sets.

comparison_dimensions.name: projection_loss_differential
comparison_dimensions.definition: Measures differences in abstracted or lost whole-relation features.

comparison_dimensions.name: projection_depth_comparison
comparison_dimensions.definition: Compares flattening depth across projection domains.

comparison_dimensions.name: recoverability_alignment
comparison_dimensions.definition: Compares recoverability class compatibility across projection domains.

comparison_dimensions.name: coherence_vs_conflict_tracking
comparison_dimensions.definition: Tracks where projection structures align or diverge without collapsing differences.

governance_rules.rule: Bridge comparisons require declared shared source relations.
Projection conflicts must be preserved rather than collapsed.
Bridge coherence cannot imply source identity or physical equivalence.
Bridge artifacts remain ANALOG_ONLY and NON_PHYSICAL.

forbidden_uses: Claiming QM-like and GR-like projections are unified.
Claiming projection coherence proves physical reality.
Treating bridge comparison as theorem evidence.
Treating retained feature overlap as source reconstruction.
